item.title: Google Bans Videostrong After Its Backdoor Turned 1.3 Million Android TV Boxes Into the XCPE Botnet (2026)
item.description:
Google has disrupted the XCPE botnet, a network of more than 1.3 million Android TV streaming boxes, and banned Chinese manufacturer Videostrong Technology Co. from producing certified Android devices, according to a report published Monday by the Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG). Google says Videostrong deliberately built the backdoor into devices it manufactured and sold access to criminal affiliates.

"We assess with high confidence that the backdoor and botnet were intentionally developed, deployed, and operated for financial gain by Videostrong Technology Co.," GTIG said.

Google also took down command-and-control servers used by more than a dozen related malware families, cutting off access to at least 10 million additional compromised devices. Those include retail set-top boxes, karaoke machines, and telehealth hardware, and Google says not all of them run Android.

Google Revokes Videostrong's Android TV License

Google has ended its relationship with Videostrong and revoked the company's license to manufacture Android TV devices with preloaded Google apps and services.

The ban extends to future affiliates, which cannot produce certified Android devices or supply software to certified vendors. Google says it changed its certification review process after finding that Videostrong used obfuscation to evade security testing and load malicious code only after a device first booted.

Japan's National Police Agency joined the operation alongside security companies Lumen, HUMAN Security, Plume, Synthient, and TrendAI. Synthient traced the backdoor to Videostrong after finding it preinstalled on a MECOOL KM9PRO Max Android TV box bought in late 2025, and the researchers found Videostrong company email addresses had been used to sign the backdoors.

XCPE did not arrive through a vulnerability or a malicious download. The malware, tracked as x.cpe and com.oemservice, sat in the firmware from the factory and ran with Android system-level privileges. Operators could use it to:

  • silently download and install additional Android apps
  • disable Google Play Protect
  • run shell commands and scripts with system privileges
  • capture screenshots and inject keystrokes
  • collect account information, device details, installed app lists, and system logs

Affiliates used the boxes for ad fraud, ran residential proxy software that routed third-party traffic through owners' connections without consent, and installed further backdoors named Moyu, Spirit, and Bird.

What Owners of Infected Android TV Boxes Can Do

The takedown disrupted XCPE's operations but did not remove the malware from infected boxes, Google says. The backdoor reinstalls itself from the /oem/ partition when it is deleted, so removing the malicious apps alone does not clean a device. Owners of affected boxes have two options:

  1. Install clean firmware on the box to remove the infection.
  2. Disconnect the box from the internet to stop further malicious activity if clean firmware is not available.

Google says Videostrong placed the malware in different device brands and models over multiple years, but the company has not published a full list of affected products beyond the MECOOL box identified by Synthient.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Google Bans Videostrong After Its Backdoor Turned 1.3 Million Android TV Boxes Into the XCPE Botnet appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Microsoft Says Windows 11 26H2 Makes 8 GB PCs Up to 20% More Responsive and 40% Faster at Multitasking (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft has detailed a set of memory management changes in Windows 11 that it says make PCs with 8 GB of RAM up to 20 percent more responsive and 40 percent faster at multitasking, according to a Windows Experience Blog post by Pavan Davuluri, executive vice president of Windows and Devices. The improvements ship in Windows 11 26H2, build 26300.9818 or later.

The post follows a renewed push on memory optimization that Microsoft started earlier in 2026. Copilot+ PCs, which Microsoft continues to promote, require at least 16 GB of RAM, while memory prices keep climbing on demand from AI infrastructure.

Windows 11 Memory Changes for 8 GB PCs

Most of the work adjusts how Windows 11 handles memory on lower-specced hardware instead of adding features. Microsoft lists these changes:

  • Windows 11 keeps up to 2 GB more active data in memory before moving it to slower storage.
  • Windows connects directly to Microsoft Edge when the browser is already running in the background, which Microsoft says lets Edge launch up to 33 percent faster.
  • Microsoft Teams can enable Efficiency Mode by default on 8 GB machines, and the company says Teams then launches up to 20 percent faster.
  • Widgets load only when they are used instead of running all the time.
  • Edge puts inactive tabs to sleep after 15 minutes by default, down from two hours.

Third-party apps can use the same memory tweaks, according to Microsoft.

The blog post also cites benchmark data from research Microsoft commissioned, comparing 2026 Windows machines with models from 2021. In that report, a 2026 Dell XPS 13 with 8 GB of RAM performed about as well as a 2021 Dell XPS 13 with 16 GB across selected workloads. Microsoft's reading of the result is that "the complete PC, not memory capacity alone, shapes the experience."

Davuluri drew a line for heavier use as well. He described 8 GB as "a great fit for the things they do every day" for everyday users, while workloads such as 3D modeling, advanced video editing, or large-scale data processing "benefit from 16 GB of memory or more," according to the post.

How to Get the 8 GB Improvements on Windows 11

The gains depend on both the Windows 11 version and on app updates, so owners of 8 GB PCs need both parts current:

  1. Confirm the PC runs Windows 11 26H2, build 26300.9818 or later, and install pending updates through Windows Update.
  2. Update Microsoft apps such as Edge and Teams, since Microsoft says "some improvements arrive through app updates or through Microsoft Store."
  3. Review Edge tab behavior after updating. Tabs that sleep after 15 minutes free memory sooner but need to reload when reopened.

The 20 and 40 percent figures are Microsoft's own claims, and the commissioned benchmark covers selected workloads only. Microsoft has not said whether PCs on Windows 11 versions older than 26H2 will receive the same memory changes.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Microsoft Says Windows 11 26H2 Makes 8 GB PCs Up to 20% More Responsive and 40% Faster at Multitasking appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Rockstar Confirms GTA 6 Preload Starts November 10 With a Download of Up to 212 GB (2026)
item.description:
Rockstar Games has confirmed that digital preloading for Grand Theft Auto VI begins on Tuesday, November 10, and that the preload file requires up to 212 GB "depending on your device," according to a post on the Rockstar Newswire. GTA 6 launches globally on November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S.

The PS5 date is earlier than some buyers expected. Pre-order forms had listed November 12 as the preload start, and Rockstar has now clarified that digital preloading on PS5 opens at midnight local time on November 10. Code-in-box versions for both consoles "should" be available from retailers beginning November 12, Rockstar says.

GTA 6 Preload and Launch Times on PS5 and Xbox

The two consoles follow different schedules. PS5 preloading starts at local midnight in each time zone, while Xbox Series X and S preloading opens at the same moment worldwide, 12 a.m. GMT on November 10. In the US, that puts the Xbox preload at 4 p.m. PT and 7 p.m. ET on November 9.

  • PS5 preload: 12 a.m. local time on November 10, which is 9 p.m. PST on November 9 in Los Angeles
  • Xbox Series X and S preload: 12 a.m. GMT on November 10, which is 8 a.m. in Beijing, 9 a.m. in Tokyo and Seoul, and 11 a.m. AEST in Melbourne
  • Launch on both platforms: midnight local time on November 19, which is 9 p.m. PST on November 18 in Los Angeles

Earlier PlayStation Store data had put the PS5 download at 210 GB. Rockstar's figure of up to 212 GB covers the preload file, PS5 and Xbox sizes may differ slightly, and final install sizes can differ from preload downloads. "So make sure you've got ample space to begin pre-loading as soon as possible," Rockstar said.

Players who want to start on launch night should prepare before November 10:

  1. Free up at least 212 GB of storage on the console before preloading opens.
  2. Note the preload start for the platform, local midnight on PS5 or 12 a.m. GMT on Xbox Series X and S.
  3. Expect codes for code-in-box physical editions from retailers from November 12, two days after digital preloading begins.

GTA 6 Cover Art Poster and Map of Leonida

Rockstar will add a printable GTA 6 cover art poster and map of Leonida as a free digital download on its official site on November 19. A double-sided physical version will follow shortly after launch on the Rockstar Store, priced at $0.99 on its own or free with any purchase from the store.

Rockstar has published a preload FAQ on its support site, but the publisher has not listed separate final install sizes for PS5 and Xbox Series X and S.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Rockstar Confirms GTA 6 Preload Starts November 10 With a Download of Up to 212 GB appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Federal judge sends Zula Casino lawsuit back to Georgia state court (2026)
item.description:
Federal judge Clay D. Land sent Georgia Gambling Recovery LLC’s lawsuit against Zula Casino’s operator and two Blazesoft companies back to Georgia state court on November 3, 2026. His order grants the plaintiff’s request to return the case to the State Court of Muscogee County.

The case names Blazesoft Ltd., Blazegames, Inc. and SCPS LLC, which operates as Zula Casino. The defendants moved the action to the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Georgia in June. The federal case carries the number 4:26-cv-00914-CDL. The docket identifies the defendants and removal date.

Why the arbitration agreement failed to establish federal jurisdiction

The companies relied on the New York Convention, an international agreement concerning arbitration agreements and foreign arbitral awards, to establish federal jurisdiction. Land found that Georgia Gambling Recovery had neither signed the arbitration agreement nor agreed to be bound by it. He also rejected the defendants’ argument that Georgia law allowed them to enforce the agreement against the company.

Georgia Gambling Recovery seeks relief under the state’s gambling-loss recovery statute. Land explained that its asserted right to relief arose from that statute, rather than a contract containing an arbitration clause. He concluded that the defendants had failed to establish federal jurisdiction and directed the clerk to remand the action. The November 3 order sets out his reasoning.

Why the VGW, Blitz and Dabble cases stayed in federal court

On October 28, Land had kept the same plaintiff’s separate cases against VGW, Blitz Studios and Dabble in federal court. Those cases involved diversity jurisdiction, which depends on the parties’ citizenship and the amount in dispute. The court found those requirements satisfied. The Blazesoft case relied on a different jurisdictional basis through the arbitration convention. The October 28 order covers those three cases.

The November 3 ruling places the gambling-loss claim back before the State Court of Muscogee County for further proceedings on the underlying allegations.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Federal judge sends Zula Casino lawsuit back to Georgia state court appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Microsoft Upgrades Outlook Search With Seven Ranked Results and a Small Language Model Ranker (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft has introduced a revamped search experience in Outlook that shows seven ranked results instead of three and handles common stop words better, according to a Microsoft blog post. The new ranking layout is available across Outlook versions, including the new Outlook and Classic Outlook.

The redesign targets a long-standing problem with Outlook search: irrelevant emails show up in the results while the message a user actually needs is missing. Microsoft says it focused on three areas while building the new search, namely better ranking, improved performance when connectivity is poor, and a tighter feedback loop.

How the New Outlook Search Ranks Emails

A search in Outlook now lists seven ranked emails at the top rather than three. Microsoft ranks these messages by recency, sender, how much the message has been interacted with, and other signals. Showing more ranked messages is meant to surface the relevant email more often, and the larger set also helps Microsoft improve its ranking systems over time.

Stop words get different treatment as well. Words such as "the," "and," and "is" used to pull unrelated emails into the results, which users then had to scroll through in chronological order. Microsoft illustrates the change in its blog post with a search for "the FY27 budget," comparing what the old and the new Outlook search return for the same query.

The ranking comes from a small language model built specifically for Outlook. Microsoft trained it through distillation, a method in which a smaller model is built under the supervision of a larger one. That keeps search lightweight, because Outlook does not need to run a large model each time it ranks emails.

Classic Outlook Gets Offline Fallback and Faster Results First

Classic Outlook now falls back automatically to locally indexed content when the connection is poor, so searches still return results from mail stored on the device.

The same fallback is coming to the new Outlook, but Microsoft says it will ship later. Classic Outlook users should also see faster search results, and the company states that recent improvements reduced latency for the slowest 5% of Outlook searches.

Users can verify the changes in their own mailbox:

  1. Run a search that includes common words, for example a phrase that starts with "the," and check whether unrelated emails still appear at the top.
  2. Look for seven ranked emails above the regular results instead of three.
  3. In Classic Outlook, run a search on a slow or unstable connection to confirm that locally indexed results still appear.

Microsoft lists the tighter feedback loop as one of the three goals of the redesign and is asking Outlook users for feedback on the new results. No release date has been given for the local index fallback in the new Outlook.

item.title: Apple Will Check Public iCloud Share Links for Harmful Content Starting With iOS 27.3 (2026)
item.description:
Apple will start checking iCloud content shared through public links for "harmful content" with version 27.3 of iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS, according to a new Apple support page published on Tuesday. The checks apply only to items shared with the "Anyone with the Link" option, not to content shared directly with specific people.

The 27.3 releases went out to developers in beta on Tuesday, and a general release is expected in December. Apple has not said whether the checks are already active in the beta builds.

The policy reaches iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Vision Pro users at the same version number, so anyone who creates public iCloud links on those devices is covered once the 27.3 updates are installed.

Apple's New Rules for Anyone With the Link Sharing in iCloud

"Items shared using Anyone with the Link will be checked by Apple for harmful content," the support page states. Apple does not define harmful content on the page. The company also has not explained how the checks work, or whether human moderators, automated systems, or both will identify and remove content.

Apple says it can access items shared this way. The public sharing option removes end-to-end encryption from the shared item, even when Advanced Data Protection, Apple's optional end-to-end encryption feature for supported iCloud data, remains enabled on the account.

When harmful content is found, Apple reserves the right to move, refuse, modify, remove, or delete it at any time, according to the support page. The company says it may also block or disable accounts associated with that content and reserves the right to involve law enforcement when necessary. Apple does not list which content types fall under the policy.

How iCloud Users Can Review Their Public Links

The checks are tied to the sharing method, not to iCloud storage as a whole. iCloud users who rely on public links can review their sharing habits before the 27.3 updates reach their devices:

  1. Go through iCloud items that are currently shared with Anyone with the Link and decide whether each link still needs to be public.
  2. Share sensitive items directly with specific people instead of creating a public link, since the checks cover only links that anyone can open.
  3. Keep in mind that Advanced Data Protection does not protect items shared with Anyone with the Link, because that option removes end-to-end encryption from the shared item.

The support page ties the checks to Anyone with the Link sharing only. Apple has not said whether items that were shared publicly before iOS 27.3 will also be checked once the update is installed, and the company has not given an exact release date beyond the expected December rollout.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Apple Will Check Public iCloud Share Links for Harmful Content Starting With iOS 27.3 appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Google Will Turn Gemini Gems Into Skills on November 17 and Remove the Old Gems on December 17 (2026)
item.description:
Google will replace Gems in Gemini with skills on November 17, 2026, for personal Google accounts of users aged 18 and older, and the original Gems will be removed from those accounts on December 17, according to Google. The company says it will migrate existing Gems automatically, but files attached to Gems face new limits and some file types will be deleted.

On November 17, Gems transition to skills. The original Gems stay visible for reference, but users can no longer use, edit, or create them. On December 17, Gems disappear from the account entirely.

Skills work differently from Gems. A Gem has to be opened directly, while a skill can be called up anywhere in Gemini, including in the middle of an existing chat, by typing a slash followed by the skill name.

Google plans to switch that trigger to the at sign. item.title: Epic Games Raises Fortnite Crew to Up to 1,600 V-Bucks a Month From December 5 and Ends Monthly Skins (2026)
item.description:
Epic Games is changing the Fortnite Crew subscription on December 5, raising the base monthly V-Bucks grant back to 1,000 and adding higher amounts for long-term subscribers, according to a post on the official Fortnite blog. The price of Fortnite Crew stays the same, but the monthly Crew skin, one of the subscription's main perks, ends after December.

Fortnite Crew paid 1,000 V-Bucks per month for most of its existence. Earlier this year, Epic cut the grant to 800 following its V-Bucks price increases.

Fortnite Crew V-Bucks Tiers and New XP Bonus

From December 5, the monthly V-Bucks amount depends on how long a player has been subscribed without a break:

  • 1,000 V-Bucks per month as the new base amount
  • 1,200 V-Bucks per month after at least 3 consecutive months
  • 1,400 V-Bucks per month after 6 consecutive months
  • 1,600 V-Bucks per month from 12 months onward, the maximum

At the top level, a long-term subscriber receives twice the 800 V-Bucks that Crew paid after this year's cut. Epic assigns the tiers automatically to current subscribers on December 5.

Current subscribers will be placed in a bronze, silver, or gold tier based on the number of consecutive months they have been subscribed in the last year as of December 5. Lapsed subscribers who resubscribe between December 5 and December 31 get a starting tier based on their most recent continuous subscription period over the past 12 months, Epic says.

Crew members also get faster progression. Subscribers will earn 20% more XP than players without Crew, while non-subscribers still receive a 10% XP bonus when they play on the same team as a subscriber.

Fortnite Crew Monthly Skins End After December

The monthly skin is the one perk going away. Crew skins have never been offered any other way, including in the regular Item Shop, which made them a key reason to subscribe. After December, subscribers will no longer receive one each month, which makes December the final month with a Crew skin included.

Epic is unlocking all remaining Legacy Styles in December for everyone who owns the related cosmetics, whether or not they are still subscribed. Legacy Styles are alternate color styles for certain Crew skins, back blings, and pickaxes that were previously unlocked over months of subscription.

Everything else stays in place. Crew continues to include the Battle Pass, Music Pass, LEGO Pass, and Rocket Pass Premium without separate purchases.

Former subscribers who want their past subscription history to count toward a higher starting tier need to resubscribe between December 5 and December 31. Epic has not said whether earlier Crew skins will ever be sold in the Item Shop once the monthly skins end.

item.title: Nintendo Sold 6.49 Million Switch 2 Consoles in Six Months, Down From 10.36 Million a Year Earlier (2026)
item.description:
Nintendo sold 6.49 million Switch 2 consoles between April 1 and September 30, 2026, down from 10.36 million in the same period a year earlier, according to the company's latest financial results.

The drop of 3.87 million units, roughly 37 percent, covers the first half of Nintendo's fiscal year and mostly predates the gaming console's $50 price increase in the US, Canada, and Europe.

Nintendo also lowered its expectations for the full year. The company now forecasts 16.5 million Switch 2 units sold by March 31, 2027, compared with 19.86 million in the previous 12-month period, a reduction of 16.9 percent.

Nintendo Switch 2 Hardware and Software Sales

Nintendo labels the reporting window FY27 Q1 to Q2, the first six months of its fiscal year ending March 31, 2027. The original Switch sold 1.27 million units in the same six months, down 32.7 percent. That decline is expected for a console in its final years.

The Switch 2 numbers stand out because the console's first year went so well. It sold 19.8 million units in that period, which is more than the original Switch managed in its first full year (around 17.7 million). The original Switch then doubled that figure in its second year, a pattern the Switch 2 forecast does not follow.

Software sales moved in the other direction:

  • Switch 2 games rose 18.8 percent, from 20.62 million to 24.49 million units
  • Switch games rose 6.8 percent, from 61.56 million to 65.73 million units

Nintendo says in its report that consumers continued to adopt the Switch 2 even though hardware sales declined year over year, and it credits the release of new titles for that.

Switch 2 Price Increase and the Holiday Quarter

Nintendo announced the Switch 2 price increase in May 2026. Japan saw the higher price immediately, while the US, Canada, and Europe moved to the new price on September 1, 2026. The console now costs $500, up from its $450 launch price. Nintendo attributed the change to "changes in market conditions."

Because the reporting period ended on September 30, the results show only one month of sales at the higher price in most Western markets. The reduced forecast is Nintendo's first indication of how it expects the holiday quarter to go.

For buyers, the current situation is straightforward. The Switch 2 costs $500 in the US, and Nintendo's sales growth now comes from software, including new releases such as the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which launched this week.

Nintendo has not broken down how much of the hardware decline it attributes to the price increase, and the effect of the $500 price on holiday sales will only show up in the company's next quarterly results.

item.title: Microsoft Will Add Opt-In Copilot Answers to the New Windows 11 Search Later This Year (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft will add an optional Copilot integration to the rebuilt Search experience in Windows 11, with the feature starting to roll out to select markets later this year, the company says. Microsoft states that the Copilot option will be opt-in, which means Windows 11 users who do not turn it on will not see Copilot inside the taskbar Search interface.

The announcement follows the overhauled Windows Search that Microsoft introduced in October. Microsoft says the new Search will begin rolling out before the end of 2026.

Copilot Integration in the New Windows 11 Search

Microsoft describes the integration in a short statement: "We will also begin adding the option to integrate the new Copilot with Search on the taskbar, so you can get quick answers inline from Search, and if you want to have a richer conversation, you can jump from Search directly to the full Copilot app." The company adds that "this experience will be opt-in, and will first start rolling out to select markets later this year."

Two modes are planned once the option is enabled:

  • quick Copilot answers shown inline in the taskbar Search results
  • a direct handoff from Search to the full Copilot app for longer conversations

The rebuilt Windows Search itself was designed from the ground up. Microsoft says it returns more accurate file and app results and can change settings or start actions that the user asks for. Users can also answer text messages, open apps, and preview images, files, and rich content without leaving the Search interface. The new version uses less web content and relies on native Windows UI frameworks, which Microsoft says makes the interface faster.

Why the Opt-In Model Matters for Windows 11 Users

The new Search builds on Ask Copilot, an experience Microsoft announced last year that never shipped outside of preview builds. Testing of Ask Copilot was paused over the summer. The new Windows Search looks almost identical to it.

One difference is control. Ask Copilot had no option to turn off the Copilot integration in its interface. The new Windows Search keeps the same design but makes Copilot a choice rather than a fixed part of the experience. Earlier this year, Microsoft also said it would reduce the amount of Copilot integration across Windows.

For users, the practical result is simple. Anyone who does not want AI answers in taskbar Search does not have to change anything, because the integration stays off unless it is turned on. Users who want Copilot answers in Search will have to wait until the option reaches their market and then enable it.

Microsoft has not listed the select markets that get the Copilot option first, and the company has not said where the opt-in setting will appear in Windows 11 or when it will reach additional languages and regions.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Microsoft Will Add Opt-In Copilot Answers to the New Windows 11 Search Later This Year appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Warby Parker Opens Pre-Orders for Its Android XR Intelligent Eyewear on November 12 (2026)
item.description:
Warby Parker will open pre-orders for its first Android XR smart glasses, called Intelligent Eyewear, on November 12, the company confirmed during its third quarter 2026 earnings call. The glasses are part of a joint effort between Samsung and Google and run on Google's Android XR platform.

Warby Parker co-founder and co-CEO Dave Gilboa said customers can expect their orders to arrive during the holiday season. An exact shipping date has not been announced.

Samsung's Android XR Glasses and the Eyewear Partners

Samsung announced at the Galaxy Z Fold 8 launch earlier this year that its Android XR smart glasses would be available later in 2026. The company said at the time that it was developing the glasses together with the eyewear brands Warby Parker and Gentle Monster.

Samsung did not share a launch date or other availability details at that event. Since then, a leak has shown a range of designs and styles for the upcoming Samsung Galaxy smart glasses, but Warby Parker's earnings call is the first source to put a date on sales.

Gentle Monster has not announced when its version of the glasses will open for pre-order. Warby Parker's November 12 date is the first confirmed purchase window for the platform.

The glasses use Qualcomm hardware. Unlike Samsung's Galaxy XR headset, they do not include a built-in display, which places them closer to camera and audio glasses than to a headset. Leaked designs have shown Samsung working on two variants, one with a built-in camera and one without. Reports also point to built-in speakers for audio, microphones for voice commands and calls, and an LED indicator on the camera model that signals when the glasses are recording. Samsung has not confirmed these specifications.

Pricing and Availability Still Unconfirmed

No official price has been published for Intelligent Eyewear or for Samsung's own model. Samsung has previously said the glasses will fall into a "reasonably premium" price range. The first phase of availability is expected to be limited to the US and South Korea.

Buyers who are considering the glasses can act on the confirmed details:

  1. Check Warby Parker's store on November 12, when pre-orders open and pricing is expected to become visible.
  2. Decide between the camera and non-camera variants once the final specifications are listed, since the camera model carries a recording indicator and different privacy considerations.
  3. Factor in the holiday delivery window, as Warby Parker has not given a specific shipping date.

The glasses will be among the first Android XR smart glasses on the market and will compete with Meta's Ray-Ban smart glasses.

Warby Parker has not said which countries the November 12 pre-orders cover, and neither Samsung nor Gentle Monster has confirmed when their versions of the Android XR glasses will go on sale.

item.title: Discord Is Rebuilding Its Desktop App in Rust, With the New Client Using 290 MB of RAM (2026)
item.description:
Discord is rebuilding its desktop app in Rust and replacing the Electron framework the current client is built on, according to Discord CTO Stanislav Vishnevskiy.

In posts on X on November 4 and 5, Vishnevskiy showed the new client running on Windows 11 with 290.2 MB of memory in use while active, and he said Discord wants to start testing it with users soon. No release date has been given.

The current Electron client regularly uses more than 500 MB of memory on Windows. Electron is built on Chromium, so every Electron app ships with what amounts to its own browser engine, and that overhead is what the move to Rust is meant to remove.

How Discord's Rust Client Is Built

Discord has used Rust since 2018. Vishnevskiy says a large part of the company's infrastructure, its voice technology, and some of the current client already run on Rust, and that moving the whole client to Rust was "the holy grail." With the rebuild, Electron goes away, and so does React Native.

The change also affects mobile. Discord's mobile apps keep their native interface but will share app code with the desktop client through Rust.

Some developers expected Discord to use Tauri, an open-source framework for desktop and mobile apps. Vishnevskiy says the company is using GPUI, a framework written in Rust, with Discord's own patches applied on top.

Startup speed is the second claim. Vishnevskiy showed two Lenovo ThinkPads running Windows 11 side by side, one with the current client and one with the Rust version, and the new client opened noticeably faster. These figures come from Discord itself. Independent measurements are not available yet, since the client is not in public testing.

Why Lower Memory Use Matters for Discord Users

The rebuild comes while memory prices remain high, and buyers of new PCs often end up with 8GB of RAM to keep costs down. Microsoft is working on the same problem from the operating system side and has published Windows 11 26H2 performance claims for 8 GB PCs.

Electron stayed popular because it lets developers keep one codebase for Windows, macOS, and Linux. Slack, Microsoft Teams, and Visual Studio Code are built on it as well. Discord now joins the developers who decided the efficiency cost was too high.

Users who want a baseline before the new client arrives can check how much memory Discord uses today:

  1. Press Ctrl+Shift+Esc to open Task Manager.
  2. Select the Processes tab and expand the Discord entry.
  3. Note the combined value in the Memory column while Discord is active.

Discord has not announced when testing of the Rust client will begin, which platforms get it first, or whether early builds will be opt-in.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Discord Is Rebuilding Its Desktop App in Rust, With the New Client Using 290 MB of RAM appeared first on gHacks.

item.description:
Blizzard says World of Warcraft: Forever has delivered the biggest launch in World of Warcraft history by peak concurrent players, according to a post on the official Warcraft social media channels. item.title: Google, Meta, and TikTok Sue California Over AB 1709 Ban on Addictive Feeds for Children Under 16 (2026)
item.description:
Google, Meta, and TikTok have filed separate lawsuits against California over Assembly Bill 1709, a state law that restricts addictive social media features for children under 16. The complaints, filed Wednesday, argue that the law violates the First Amendment and conflicts with Section 230. The law is scheduled to take effect on January 1, 2027.

Governor Gavin Newsom signed AB 1709 on September 10 as part of a broader package covering social media and AI chatbot safety.

What California's AB 1709 Restricts

AB 1709 targets three features that the law defines as "psychologically exploitative features":

  • personalized feeds
  • endless scrolling
  • autoplay videos

Platforms covered by the law must also take reasonable steps to verify the ages of their users. California's goal is to stop companies from using features designed to keep children scrolling after they meant to put the phone down.

How Google, Meta, and TikTok Are Challenging the Law

The three companies argue in their filings that California is dictating how they present content and replacing parents' judgment with the state's own. Each company frames the challenge slightly differently.

Meta says the state cannot override its editorial decisions about how posts are organized and displayed. TikTok says the restrictions interfere with free expression and parental choice. Google argues that the rules could undermine systems that help children find appropriate videos, and says parents should decide what is appropriate for their families, pointing to its existing parental controls.

"Overly broad laws like this actually break the systems we've built to help kids find high-quality, age-appropriate videos," Google spokesman José Castañeda said.

The office of California Attorney General Rob Bonta said it is reviewing the lawsuits and will defend the state's child-protection laws.

Opposition is not limited to the platforms. The Electronic Frontier Foundation warns that age checks could push all users to hand over more personal information, and argues that removing recommendation tools could effectively shut young people out of online communities.

The lawsuits follow Meta's August agreement to pay up to $18 billion and change how teenagers use Facebook and Instagram to settle child-safety claims brought by states. Those changes include default time limits and mandatory scrolling breaks. Australia was the first country to pass an under-16 social media law, and Reddit has challenged that ban in Australia's High Court.

Nothing changes for California users yet. Parents who want limits before the law takes effect still have to rely on the parental controls each platform already offers, such as the ones Google points to in its argument. Age verification under AB 1709 would add a new data collection step for all users if the law survives, which is the trade-off the Electronic Frontier Foundation highlights.

No ruling has been issued, and the companies have not said whether they will ask the court to block AB 1709 before its January 1, 2027 start date.

item.title: WhatsApp Events Now Lets Users Invite People Without a WhatsApp Account and Adds an Events Home Hub (2026)
item.description:
Meta is rolling out an updated Events feature in WhatsApp that lets users invite people who do not have a WhatsApp account, according to an announcement on the WhatsApp blog. The update also adds a new Events Home hub for creating invites and managing RSVPs, and Meta says it will reach WhatsApp users over the coming weeks.

Guests without the app can open a shared event link, see the details, and RSVP without downloading WhatsApp. Meta pitches the change as timed for holiday meetups.

WhatsApp Events Now Reaches People Without an Account

The workflow is short. An organizer creates an event, adds a cover photo, and shares the event link. Recipients who use WhatsApp see the invite as usual, while people outside the platform can view the event and reply through the link.

"With Events on WhatsApp, your invite can now reach everyone, even friends who don't have a WhatsApp account," Meta writes in the blog post.

Events Home is the second part of the update. Meta describes it as "your one-stop to create and send customized invites and manage RSVPs." The hub supports:

  • customized invites created and sent from one place
  • RSVP tracking for each event
  • custom reminders for guests
  • an option for guests to add a plus one
  • a list of past and upcoming events, including ones the user created or was invited to

Before this update, WhatsApp users often organized gatherings in regular chats. Events Home pulls invitations, replies, and reminders into a single view instead.

Privacy Rules for Guests Outside WhatsApp

Opening events to people outside the platform raises an obvious question about what those guests can see. Meta addresses it with two rules.

When a user invites guests they are not connected to on WhatsApp, the organizer's phone number is not shared with those guests. Meta also says the address of an event will not be shown to people who do not use WhatsApp until they have RSVP'd to the invitation. These rules sit on top of the end-to-end encryption WhatsApp already uses across the service.

Users who want to check the feature once it arrives can follow these steps:

  1. Update WhatsApp to the latest version from the app store.
  2. Open Settings and select Events to view Events Home.
  3. Create an event, add a cover photo, and share the event link with guests.
  4. Track replies and set custom reminders from Events Home.

Organizers who share an event link widely should keep in mind that anyone with the link can view the event details, and the address becomes visible to non-WhatsApp guests once they RSVP.

Meta says the updated Events feature is rolling out over the coming weeks and has not listed a date for specific countries or platforms.

item.title: Microsoft Re-Releases KB5002934 for Excel 2016 After a Later Update Broke Copy and Paste Again (2016)
item.description:
Microsoft has re-released the KB5002934 update for Excel 2016 after a later update brought back a bug that breaks copy and paste in some workbooks. According to the updated KB5002934 support page, the new release moves Excel 2016 to build 16.0.5574.1006 and fixes a paste failure that returned in build 16.0.5574.1005.

The bug affects workbooks that contain conditional formatting. In those files, paste operations might fail. Microsoft first broke copy and paste in Excel in September, shipped a fix, and then saw the same problem return with another update this month.

The re-released update keeps the KB5002934 number, but it is not the same package that shipped last month.

What Changed in the Re-Released KB5002934 Update

Microsoft explains the change directly on the support page. The page originally described build 16.0.5574.1005, and Microsoft has since updated the release to build 16.0.5574.1006 without assigning a new KB number. According to the company, build 16.0.5574.1006 "includes all security updates for Microsoft Excel 2016" and also fixes the reintroduced issue "in which paste operations might fail if the workbook contains conditional formatting."

Two consecutive updates have now broken the same Excel function. A re-release under an existing KB number is uncommon for Microsoft, and the company has not explained how the paste problem made its way back into Excel after the September fix.

The scope is narrow. Only Excel 2016 is affected, which is an older release of the spreadsheet app, so the number of impacted users is smaller than a bug in a current Microsoft 365 build would reach. Organizations that still run Excel 2016 on managed PCs are the main group that needs to act.

How Excel 2016 Users Can Restore Copy and Paste

Excel 2016 users who saw paste operations fail in workbooks with conditional formatting should move to the revised release. The fix is part of the security update itself, so there is no separate hotfix to hunt down.

  1. Confirm that the affected installation is Excel 2016 and not a newer Office or Microsoft 365 version.
  2. Check the Excel build number. Build 16.0.5574.1005 contains the reintroduced paste bug.
  3. Install the re-released KB5002934 update so that Excel 2016 reaches build 16.0.5574.1006.
  4. Open a workbook that uses conditional formatting and test a paste operation to confirm the fix.

Administrators who deployed the original KB5002934 package last month should treat the revised release as a new deployment, since the build number changed even though the KB number did not. Skipping the update is not a practical workaround, because build 16.0.5574.1006 also carries all current security updates for Excel 2016.

Microsoft has not said why the paste bug returned or what it is changing to prevent a third regression in Excel 2016.

item.title: Mullvad shuts down its public encrypted DNS service: switch to Quad9 or another resolver now (2026)
item.description:
Mullvad's free public encrypted DNS service, the DNS over HTTPS and DNS over TLS resolvers at dns.mullvad.net and its five filtering variants, was scheduled to be discontinued on November 2, 2026. Mullvad now sponsors Quad9 instead and recommends it as the replacement. Anyone who typed a Mullvad DNS hostname into a browser, Android Private DNS, a router or an iOS or macOS profile should switch to another resolver now.

Mullvad VPN users who rely on the app's built-in DNS inside the tunnel are not the target of this change. This post covers what was shut down, why, which settings to change, verified replacement addresses, and how to confirm which resolver a device really uses.

What Mullvad shut down and why

Mullvad is retiring its public encrypted DNS service only, not its VPN. Mullvad announced the move on its blog on September 3, 2026, and its DNS over HTTPS and DNS over TLS help page states that the service "will be discontinued on November 2, 2026."

The company gives two reasons. First, the servers add nothing for its VPN customers, because VPN traffic is already encrypted and the VPN's own resolver handles queries. Second, it considers running a privacy-focused public resolver a specialized job and prefers to fund Quad9, which it calls the leader in the field, rather than duplicate that work. Mullvad says it will financially support Quad9 but does not name an amount.

The service launched as a free alternative for people who wanted encrypted DNS without a VPN. In 2023, ghacks reported that Mullvad's public encrypted DNS servers moved to RAM-only operation; that infrastructure is what is going away.

Which Mullvad DNS settings stop working

Every manual configuration that points to a Mullvad DNS hostname or address is affected. The help page lists these six resolvers:

  • dns.mullvad.net (194.242.2.2): no blocking
  • adblock.dns.mullvad.net (194.242.2.3): ads and trackers
  • base.dns.mullvad.net (194.242.2.4): ads, trackers and malware
  • extended.dns.mullvad.net (194.242.2.5): base plus social media
  • family.dns.mullvad.net (194.242.2.6): base plus adult content and gambling
  • all.dns.mullvad.net (194.242.2.9): all of the above

The older hostnames doh.mullvad.net and dot.mullvad.net, which the help page already listed as replaced, should be removed as well. Mullvad's blog adds three platform notes:

  • Mullvad Browser: users on the default DNS over HTTPS setting or the included ad-blocking option are moved to Quad9 automatically. Custom settings are not changed, so anyone who picked base, extended or family should switch back to the default.
  • iOS and macOS: Mullvad DNS configuration profiles stop working. Delete them and install a Quad9 profile instead.
  • Everything else (browsers, Android, routers, Windows): replace the hostname or DoH URL by hand.

Replacement resolvers with DoH and DoT addresses

Quad9 is the replacement Mullvad recommends, and it is the closest fit in terms of privacy policy. Quad9 is a Swiss public-benefit not-for-profit foundation, and its privacy policy states that it "does not collect or record user IP addresses." Its default service blocks malicious domains and validates DNSSEC. ghacks covered the launch of Quad9 in 2017.

All addresses below come from each provider's own documentation:

Resolver DNS over HTTPS URL DNS over TLS / Android Private DNS hostname
Quad9 (malware blocking) https://dns.quad9.net/dns-query dns.quad9.net
Quad9 (no blocking) https://dns10.quad9.net/dns-query dns10.quad9.net
AdGuard DNS (ad blocking) https://dns.adguard-dns.com/dns-query dns.adguard-dns.com
DNS4EU (ad blocking) https://noads.joindns4.eu/dns-query noads.joindns4.eu
Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query one.one.one.one

The plain IPv4 addresses are 9.9.9.9 and 149.112.112.112 for Quad9, 94.140.14.14 and 94.140.15.15 for AdGuard DNS, 86.54.11.13 and 86.54.11.213 for DNS4EU, and 1.1.1.1 and 1.0.0.1 for Cloudflare.

Which one replaces which Mullvad tier:

  • dns.mullvad.net: Quad9 no-blocking or Cloudflare.
  • adblock, base or all: AdGuard DNS or DNS4EU ad blocking, both of which filter ads and trackers. AdGuard says it processes no personal data on its public servers; DNS4EU, operated by Whalebone in the Czech Republic, says client IPs are anonymised before logging.
  • family: DNS4EU's child protection variant (child.joindns4.eu).

Cloudflare says it keeps no source IPs in non-volatile storage and deletes truncated IPs within 25 hours. Our older look at AdGuard DNS and its filtering explains the blocking approach in more detail. To enter any of these in a browser, follow our guide to enabling DNS over HTTPS in Chrome, Brave, Edge and Firefox.

How to check which resolver a device uses

The quickest check is the provider's own test page, opened on the device you changed. Quad9's on.quad9.net answers yes or no, and Cloudflare's one.one.one.one/help runs a set of tests that show whether the connection to 1.1.1.1 works.

  1. Open the browser's secure DNS setting first. A browser DoH provider overrides the system resolver, and Quad9 notes that Firefox and Brave may default to Cloudflare in some regions.
  2. On Windows, run ipconfig /all in a terminal and read the DNS Servers lines for the active adapter. Any 194.242.2.x address is a leftover Mullvad entry.
  3. On Android, open Settings, search for Private DNS and confirm the hostname. Replace any Mullvad hostname with one from the table above.
  4. On iOS and macOS, check the installed profiles under VPN and Device Management and remove any Mullvad DNS profile. iCloud Private Relay must be off for a third-party resolver to apply.
  5. If a VPN is active, enter the new resolver in the VPN client's custom DNS setting, because VPNs usually ignore the device setting.

Do not mix providers: Quad9's test reports "no" when a device lists a Quad9 address next to one from another resolver.

item.title: How to AirDrop on iPhone
item.description:
To AirDrop on iPhone, open the photo or file, tap the Share button, tap AirDrop and tap the person or device under People. The receiver taps Accept. Both devices need Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on, Personal Hotspot off, and must be within about 30 feet (10 meters). Contacts can find you with the default setting; anyone else needs Everyone for 10 Minutes and, from iOS 26.2, an AirDrop code.

This guide covers the current iOS 27 behavior: turning AirDrop on, sending and receiving, who can see you, where received files land, iPhone to Mac and iPhone to Android. If transfers fail, use our separate fixes for AirDrop not working or failing.

What is AirDrop?

AirDrop is Apple's wireless sharing feature that sends photos, videos, documents, contacts and links directly between nearby iPhone, iPad and Mac devices, without a cable, an upload or a messaging app. It is built into the share sheet of almost every app, so anything you can share, you can usually AirDrop.

How AirDrop works

AirDrop uses Bluetooth to find nearby devices and Wi-Fi to move the data, which is why Apple requires both to be switched on. Apple states that devices must be within 30 feet (10 meters) of one another. The transfer runs directly between the two devices rather than through a cloud server, which is why large videos often arrive faster than through a chat app.

Since iOS 17.1, a transfer that has started keeps going over the internet if you walk out of range (see the cellular section below), and since iOS 26.2, people outside your contacts are verified with a short AirDrop code.

How to turn on AirDrop on iPhone

To turn on AirDrop, open Control Center, touch and hold the connectivity controls, tap AirDrop and choose Contacts Only or Everyone for 10 Minutes. On iPhones with Face ID, Control Center opens with a swipe down from the top-right corner of the screen; on iPhones with a Home button, swipe up from the bottom edge.

  1. Open Control Center.
  2. Touch and hold the group of connectivity controls (the tile with Airplane Mode, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth).
  3. Tap AirDrop.
  4. Choose Contacts Only to be visible to people in your Contacts, or Everyone for 10 Minutes to be visible to any nearby device for a short time.

The same choice is available in Settings > General > AirDrop, which is also where the Use Cellular Data option lives. If AirDrop is not listed in Control Center at all, check Screen Time content restrictions, which can hide it on managed or children's devices.

How to AirDrop photos and files from iPhone

To AirDrop something, select the items, tap the Share button, tap AirDrop and then tap the person or device under People. Nearby contacts with AirDrop enabled appear there automatically.

  1. Open the app that holds the content, for example Photos or Files.
  2. Select the item or items. In Photos, tap Select and tap each photo; in Files, tap the More button, then Select.
  3. Tap the Share button, then tap AirDrop.
  4. Tap the person or device under People and wait for the receiver to accept.

Send to someone who is not in your contacts

Sending to a stranger takes one step on each side. The recipient opens Control Center and sets AirDrop to Everyone for 10 Minutes, then you tap their device under People. If both iPhones run iOS 26.2 or later, you are prompted for an AirDrop code: the recipient taps Get AirDrop Code and reads the code to you, and you enter it. Apple says the recipient is then added to your Other Known list for 30 days, and you can mark them as unknown in the Contacts app before that period ends.

Bring two iPhones together

If both devices run iOS 17 or later, you can hold the two iPhones close together to start an AirDrop share without opening the People list. The same gesture powers NameDrop, Apple's feature for swapping contact information instead of files.

How to receive AirDrop on iPhone

To receive AirDrop, tap Accept on the AirDrop prompt that appears on your screen; items sent between devices signed in to the same Apple Account are accepted automatically. Make sure the sender can see you first.

  1. Set AirDrop to Contacts Only if the sender is in your Contacts, or to Everyone for 10 Minutes if they are not.
  2. Keep Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on and Personal Hotspot off.
  3. Tap Accept when the prompt appears, or Decline to refuse the item.
  4. If asked, tap Get AirDrop Code and read the code to the sender.

On a child's iPhone, Communication Safety can warn about sensitive images received or sent through AirDrop, blur them and point to help resources.

AirDrop settings: who can send to you

Contacts Only is the everyday setting, Everyone for 10 Minutes switches itself off after 10 minutes, and Receiving Off hides your iPhone completely. Since iOS 16.2, Everyone for 10 Minutes falls back to Contacts Only when you are signed in to an Apple Account, or to Receiving Off when you are not. The table shows who can reach you under each setting, which is the question most AirDrop problems come down to.

Who is sending Receiving Off Contacts Only Everyone for 10 Minutes
A person saved in your Contacts No Yes Yes
A nearby iPhone you do not know (iOS 26.2 or later) No No Yes, after the AirDrop code is exchanged
A nearby Apple device you do not know (older software) No No Yes
A supported Android phone using Quick Share No No Yes
How long the setting lasts Until you change it Until you change it 10 minutes, then Contacts Only (signed in) or Receiving Off

Code-verified people sit in the Other Known list for 30 days. Apple's AirDrop documentation describes the full code flow.

Use Cellular Data and out-of-range transfers

AirDrop can finish a transfer over the internet when you move out of Bluetooth and Wi-Fi range, and it may use mobile data for that. The Use Cellular Data switch in Settings > General > AirDrop is on by default; turn it off if you want AirDrop to stay off your data plan. Background on the change is in our post on AirDrop over cellular, added in iOS 17.1.

Where do AirDrop files go on iPhone?

Photos and videos go to the Photos app; most other items are saved in or opened with the app that handles them, as Apple puts it, "in the app that they're sent from". The table maps the common item types.

Item received Where it lands on iPhone
Photos and videos Photos app, in your library and the Recents view
PDFs and documents The matching app, or the Files app if you choose to save there
Contact cards Contacts, after you confirm the new contact
Web links Opened in your browser
Notes, maps places and other app content The app the item was shared from

Is there an AirDrop history?

No, iOS has no AirDrop history or transfer log. To find something you received earlier, check Recents in Photos, the Recents and Downloads views in Files, or the app that matches the file type. A Mac is different: some received items go straight to its Downloads folder.

How to AirDrop between iPhone and Mac

To AirDrop from iPhone to Mac, use the share sheet on the iPhone and tap the Mac under People; the Mac must be awake, unlocked and set to Contacts Only or Everyone. From Mac to iPhone, use the Share menu or Finder.

  • iPhone to Mac: select the items, tap Share, tap AirDrop, tap the Mac. If both are signed in to the same Apple Account, the item is accepted automatically and most files appear in the Mac's Downloads folder.
  • Mac to iPhone: Control-click a file and choose Share > AirDrop, or open a Finder window, click AirDrop in the sidebar and drag the file onto the iPhone.
  • Mac visibility: click Control Center in the menu bar, click the arrow next to AirDrop and choose Contacts Only or Everyone.

Can you AirDrop to Android?

Yes, with select Android phones as of November 2026: Google's Quick Share can exchange files with AirDrop when the iPhone is set to Everyone for 10 Minutes. Google added the feature in November 2025, starting with Pixel phones, and widened the list in June 2026.

Maker Supported phones (Google's list, June 2026)
Google Pixel 10, 10 Pro, 10 Pro XL, 10 Pro Fold, 10a; Pixel 9, 9 Pro, 9 Pro XL, 9 Pro Fold, 9a; Pixel 8a
Samsung Galaxy S26, S26+, S26 Ultra; S25, S25+, S25 Ultra, S25 Edge; S24, S24+, S24 Ultra; Z Flip7, Z Fold7, Z Flip6, Z Fold6, Z TriFold
Other makers HONOR Magic V6; OnePlus 15; Xiaomi 17T Pro; OPPO Find X9, X9 Pro, X9 Ultra, X9s and Find N6; vivo X300, X300 Pro, X300 Ultra

The table follows Google's June 2026 expansion as listed by MacRumors. Samsung has since added more mid-range models; see Galaxy A56 and A57 AirDrop support in One UI 9. Settings needed on both sides:

  • iPhone: set AirDrop to Everyone for 10 Minutes in Control Center.
  • Android: turn on Share with Apple devices in the Quick Share settings.
  • Android, when receiving: switch Quick Share Receive mode on.
  • Send from the iPhone through the normal AirDrop share sheet; the Android phone appears under People.

For phones that are not on the list, a browser-based tool such as open source Snapdrop for Windows and Linux or a cloud link is the practical fallback.

Is AirDrop faster in iOS 27?

Apple says it is: at its WWDC keynote on June 8, 2026, Apple listed "up to 80% faster AirDrop transfers" among the iOS 27 performance changes, as reported by 9to5Mac. Apple did not say which file types, device pairs or baseline the figure refers to, so treat it as a best case rather than a typical result. Real speed still depends on the two devices, the distance between them and the Wi-Fi conditions around you. To get the new behavior, update both devices; the other iOS 27 changes are in everything new in iOS 27.

How to change your AirDrop name

Your AirDrop name is your iPhone's name, so you change it in Settings > General > About > Name. The new name shows up for senders the next time they open the AirDrop list.

  1. Open Settings and tap General.
  2. Tap About, then tap Name.
  3. Type the new name and tap Done.

Pick a name that does not reveal your full name if you use Everyone for 10 Minutes in public places, because anyone nearby can see it during that time.

How to turn off AirDrop

To turn off AirDrop, set it to Receiving Off in Control Center or in Settings > General > AirDrop. Your iPhone then disappears from other people's AirDrop lists, while you can still send items to others.

  1. Open Control Center and touch and hold the connectivity controls.
  2. Tap AirDrop, then tap Receiving Off.

To block AirDrop entirely on a child's iPhone, use Screen Time content and privacy restrictions under allowed apps; that hides AirDrop until a parent turns it back on.

AirDrop not working?

If AirDrop fails, first check that Wi-Fi and Bluetooth are on, Personal Hotspot is off and the receiver's visibility setting allows you. For everything beyond that, follow our guide to fix AirDrop when it fails or does not show up.

FAQ

Does AirDrop need Wi-Fi or internet?

AirDrop needs Wi-Fi and Bluetooth switched on, but not a Wi-Fi network or internet connection: the devices connect to each other directly. Internet only comes into play when a started transfer continues after you move out of range.

How far does AirDrop reach?

Apple states that devices must be within 30 feet (10 meters) of one another. Walls and interference shorten that in practice, so stay close when a transfer starts.

Can you AirDrop to a Windows PC?

No, Windows has no AirDrop support. Browser-based tools such as Snapdrop or PairDrop, or a cloud storage link, are the usual alternatives.

Can strangers send me pictures with AirDrop?

Only while you are set to Everyone for 10 Minutes, and you still have to tap Accept. Contacts Only, the setting iOS falls back to, blocks unknown senders.

Related: how to factory reset an iPhone, blocking account changes with Screen Time.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post How to AirDrop on iPhone appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Sony Announces a New PlayStation Portal for Japan With Extra Internal Storage for Future Functionality (2026)
item.description:
Sony has announced a new PlayStation Portal model for Japan that adds internal storage "with an eye towards future functionality," according to a post on the PlayStation Japan blog.

The revised handheld keeps the features of the original Portal and goes up for pre-order in Japan on November 13 at ¥39,980, the same price as the current model.

Sony says more information on the storage is coming and that details of the feature are still being finalized. The company has not said how much storage the new model includes.

New PlayStation Portal Storage and Region Limits

The PlayStation Portal works as a remote player. It streams PS5 games from a console at home, or through the cloud with a PlayStation Plus Premium subscription, and does not run games locally.

Sony lists no changes to the internals of the new model beyond the added storage, so running PS5 games directly on the handheld is not part of the announcement.

The original Portal was found to have about 6 GB of free space after its launch. Sony has not confirmed the capacity of the new storage or what it will be used for.

The new model is locked to Japan, like the Midnight Black PS5 announced last month:

  • the system language can only be set to Japanese
  • a Japanese PlayStation Network account is required to use the device
  • pre-orders open in Japan only, on November 13

For buyers in Japan, the choice between the two models comes down to the storage alone. Both cost ¥39,980 and offer the same remote play and cloud streaming features, so the new model adds the storage at no extra cost. Owners of the current Portal do not need to change anything, since Sony has not tied any existing feature to the new hardware.

What Buyers Outside Japan Should Know

The new model is not built for use outside Japan. The language lock and the Japanese PSN account requirement limit the device to the Japanese store and interface, and the storage has no announced use yet. Players in other regions who want a Portal today can buy the current model, which offers the same remote play and cloud streaming features.

Sony has not said whether the storage update will come to PlayStation Portal models in the US, the UK, or other regions, and the company has not given a date for the details of the future functionality.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Sony Announces a New PlayStation Portal for Japan With Extra Internal Storage for Future Functionality appeared first on gHacks.

item.description:
Google has warned Australian lawmakers that the country's proposed Digital Duty of Care legislation could force the company to block users under 18 from Gmail.

Rachel Lord, policy head for YouTube in Australia and New Zealand, raised the concern at a Senate hearing on November 9, saying age check provisions in the bill would reach email, messaging, and private file storage.

Lord described the possible result as "intrusive monitoring within private communications or file storage." The provisions in question require age checks where children risk encountering pornography.

What the Digital Duty of Care Bill Requires

The government introduced the bill on October 15. It requires online service providers to take reasonable steps to keep Australians safe, with extra protections for users under 18. Penalties reach up to AU$109.2 million (about $75.40 million), according to the government's description of the legislation.

The bill also includes these measures:

  • tools that let users choose whether algorithmically recommended content appears in their feeds
  • powers for the eSafety Commissioner to issue removal notices for nudify apps and websites
  • a 24 hour response requirement for cyberbullying and abuse complaints
  • minimum standards for platform complaint processes

The bill has passed the House of Representatives and needs cross-party support to pass the Senate.

Meta, TikTok, and Snap Raise Objections

Google was not the only company to push back. Meta, TikTok, and Snap warned that giving regulators broad discretion over harmful content could lead platforms to remove too much material in order to avoid penalties.

The bill follows Australia's ban on social media for users under 16, which took effect on December 10, 2025, and made Australia the first country to introduce such a restriction. Reddit is challenging that ban in court, calling it "ill thought out" and "inept" and arguing that Reddit is not a social media platform.

Nothing changes for Gmail users in Australia yet. The bill is not law, and Google has not announced any change to Gmail accounts for minors. Families and schools that rely on Gmail for students under 18 should follow the Senate vote, since an age check requirement on email would affect account access rather than a single feature.

Google has not said how it would verify ages in Gmail or whether school managed accounts would be treated differently if the bill passes in its current form.

item.title: Microsoft Tests a Windows 11 Sticky Keys Prompt That Can Permanently Turn Off the Shift Key Shortcut (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft is testing a new version of the Sticky Keys prompt in Windows 11 that lets users switch off the keyboard shortcut for good from the prompt itself. The change appears in a recent Windows Insider build, where the "Do you want to turn on Sticky Keys?" dialog now includes a check box that stops it from showing up again.

The prompt opens when the Shift key is pressed five times. Microsoft is giving the Filter Keys prompt, another accessibility feature with its own keyboard shortcut, the same option.

What Changes in the Windows 11 Sticky Keys Prompt

Sticky Keys lets users press modifier keys one at a time instead of holding them down together. With the feature on, Ctrl + Alt + Delete can be entered by pressing Ctrl, then Alt, then Delete.

The Shift shortcut that turns it on has been part of Windows for decades, and it fires by accident in games and creative programs where Shift gets pressed repeatedly as part of normal work.

Today, the prompt only offers a link to the Sticky Keys page in the Settings app, and stopping it for good means changing the setting there. The updated prompt in the Insider build adds:

  • a check box that prevents the Sticky Keys prompt from appearing again
  • the same check box in the Filter Keys prompt
  • the existing link to the full Sticky Keys settings, which stays in place

The feature itself is not removed. Users who rely on Sticky Keys for accessibility can still turn it on from Settings, and the Settings page keeps related controls, such as turning Sticky Keys off when two keys are pressed at the same time.

How to Disable the Sticky Keys Shortcut on Current Windows 11

The new check box is limited to Windows Insider builds for now. On release versions of Windows 11, the shortcut can be switched off in Settings:

  1. Open Settings and go to Accessibility > Keyboard > Sticky Keys.
  2. Turn off the keyboard shortcut for Sticky Keys so that pressing Shift five times no longer opens the prompt.
  3. Check the Filter Keys section under Accessibility > Keyboard as well if that prompt also appears by accident.

Users who press Shift repeatedly in games or design software gain the most from the change, since the prompt interrupts full screen apps when it appears.

Microsoft has not said which Insider build introduced the updated prompt or when the change will reach the release version of Windows 11.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Microsoft Tests a Windows 11 Sticky Keys Prompt That Can Permanently Turn Off the Shift Key Shortcut appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Google Raises the Android Auto Minimum to Android 11, Ending Support for Android 9 and Android 10 (2026)
item.description:
Google has raised the minimum requirement for Android Auto to Android 11, ending official support for phones that run Android 9 and Android 10, according to an update to the Android Auto support page. The new minimum applies to both wired and wireless Android Auto connections.

Android Auto previously supported phones running Android 9 or later. Google had started warning Android 10 users in October 2026 that their devices would soon stop working with Android Auto, and the requirement is now in effect on the support page.

Who Is Affected by the Android Auto Android 11 Requirement

Wireless Android Auto already required Android 11 or newer, so the practical impact falls on drivers who connect their phones to the car with a USB cable. Phones in that group lose official support if they meet both of these conditions:

  • the phone runs Android 9 or Android 10
  • the manufacturer offers no update to Android 11 or a later version

Android Auto puts apps such as Google Maps, Spotify, and YouTube on the car's infotainment screen, so the change affects navigation and media playback for drivers who still use older phones in the car. Some users report that Android Auto has already stopped working on their phones, which suggests the cutoff is reaching devices now.

Google has not given an exact date for when Android Auto stops working on every affected phone.

What Owners of Older Android Phones Can Do

There is no supported way around the new minimum. Owners of older phones have these options:

  1. Check the Android version in the phone's settings to confirm whether the phone runs Android 9 or Android 10.
  2. Install any pending system update, since some phones can still move to Android 11 or newer through the manufacturer.
  3. Plan to replace the phone if it cannot be updated, because unsupported phones can lose Android Auto without warning.

Cars that support Android Auto are not affected by the change on their side. The requirement is tied to the phone's software, so a newer phone restores Android Auto in the same car.

Google has not said whether apps such as Google Maps will keep working on Android 9 and Android 10 phones outside of Android Auto, and the support page does not list a timeline for the next minimum version.

item.title: Rockstar Confirms GTA 6 Runs at 30fps on All Consoles, With Ray-Traced Shadows Only on PS5 Pro (2026)
item.description:
Rockstar Games has confirmed that GTA 6 runs at 30 frames per second on every console, including the PS5 Pro. The details come from a new Rockstar blog post published as preloads opened on November 10 for players who pre-ordered the game digitally. GTA 6 launches on November 19.

Rockstar says the game was built from the ground up for the current console generation, "targeting 30 frames per second while pushing both platforms to their absolute limits." The blog post does not mention a performance mode, either at launch or in a later update.

GTA 6 on PS5 Pro, PS5, and Xbox

The frame rate is the same on the PS5 Pro, but Sony's upgraded console gets two visual extras. Rockstar lists "improved clarity through PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) and ray-traced shadows only available on PlayStation 5 Pro."

Rockstar also says the game will "play best on PlayStation 5 consoles," citing three features on the standard PS5:

  • haptic feedback integrated across the game on DualSense controllers, adjustable through the accessibility settings
  • improved spatial audio rendering that uses Tempest 3D Audio
  • improved load times

The only Xbox detail in the post concerns Xbox Cloud Gaming. GTA 6 will be playable through the cloud on Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, and Xbox One, but the cloud version uses the Series S graphics settings, so it will not look as good as the version installed on a Series X.

Preload Size and What Pre-Order Buyers Need

The preload needs up to 212 GB of free space, depending on the console. Players who bought a physical copy get a box with a download code instead of a disc, so they have to wait for the box to arrive before they can preload.

Buyers have a few days left to make room. Before the launch on November 19:

  1. Check that the console has at least 212 GB of free space, and delete or move other games if it does not.
  2. Start the preload from the PlayStation Store or Xbox Store library entry for GTA 6.
  3. Redeem the code from the box if you bought a physical copy, then start the preload the same way.

The standard edition costs $79.99, and an Ultimate Edition upgrade with extra in-game items is also available. Digital purchases made before November 20, 2026, include the Vintage Vice City Pack, a set of 1980s style outfits for Jason and Lucia. Physical pre-orders get the same pack while supplies last.

For players choosing a platform, the blog post settles the frame rate question: no console version runs above 30 frames per second. The differences between versions come down to image quality, ray-traced shadows, and controller and audio features.

Rockstar has not said whether a 60 frames per second mode could come in a later update or when a PC version of GTA 6 will be released.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Rockstar Confirms GTA 6 Runs at 30fps on All Consoles, With Ray-Traced Shadows Only on PS5 Pro appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Microsoft Will Retire Free Office 365 A1 Email for Schools, Moving Them to an A0 Plan Without Exchange or Teams (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft is retiring Office 365 A1, the free plan that gives schools, colleges, and universities web versions of Office apps, Teams, and email at no charge. The change takes effect at each institution's first renewal or extension on or after January 1, 2028, and institutions that want to keep student mailboxes will need paid licenses after that point.

Microsoft is also retiring two related programs: the Student Use Benefit, which provides student licenses at no extra charge when an institution buys qualifying faculty licenses, and free Exchange Online for Alumni, which lets graduates keep their school mailboxes. Microsoft plans a paid replacement for the alumni service.

What Replaces Office 365 A1

The free tier continues under a new name, Microsoft 365 Education A0, but it drops the services most schools rely on day to day. A0 does not include:

  • Exchange Online, the service that hosts school email
  • SharePoint Online, used for shared files and internal sites
  • Teams, used for classes, meetings, and chat

Eligibility for A0 also depends on paid faculty licensing and on students actively using Windows devices for education. Microsoft is changing storage entitlements across the education plans as well, and it is adding Microsoft 365 Education A7, a new top tier with AI, security, governance, and device management features.

Microsoft says the change reflects how institutions now evaluate AI, security, privacy, and teaching tools together. The company also pointed to "the value Microsoft 365 Education has gained since the last pricing change nearly a decade ago."

Key Dates for Schools and Universities

The retirement is spread over the next two years, and existing agreements stay valid until they run out:

  1. November 5, 2026: Office 365 A1 stopped accepting new web direct orders.
  2. May 1, 2027: partner channel sales of Office 365 A1 end.
  3. January 1, 2028: retirement begins, applied at each institution's first renewal or extension on or after that date.

The reaction in the UK has been negative. The Department for Education said it was "disappointed" by the decision, but added that it had negotiated additional concessions that give UK schools, colleges, and universities more time to move to new licensing agreements.

One industry insider estimated that losing free Microsoft hosted email could add thousands to an institution's bill, and another education organization raised concerns about affordability and equal treatment across the sector.

IT teams in education should check when their current agreement renews, since that date, not January 1, 2028, decides when the free services end for them. Institutions that depend on A1 for student email will need to budget for paid licenses or plan a move to another email provider before that renewal.

Microsoft has not published prices for the paid alumni service or said how much the new paid tiers will cost per student.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Microsoft Will Retire Free Office 365 A1 Email for Schools, Moving Them to an A0 Plan Without Exchange or Teams appeared first on gHacks.
