item.title: Firefox's Free Built-In VPN Gets Unlimited Data From November 10 Through January 31, (2027)
item.description:
Mozilla has removed the data limit on the free VPN built into Firefox for the holiday season. Everyone using the built-in VPN gets unlimited data from November 10, 2026, through January 31, 2027, according to an announcement on the Mozilla blog.

The offer requires a Mozilla account. Users sign in, turn on the VPN, and browse without a data cap for the rest of the period.

What Firefox's Built-In VPN Does

The VPN routes Firefox traffic through Mozilla's service, which makes it harder for websites to use a visitor's IP address to work out their location or link their visits across sites. Mozilla says Firefox does not sell browsing data, show ads in the VPN, or keep a record of the websites users visit.

Mozilla highlights two everyday uses:

  • hiding the sites you visit from whoever runs a public or shared WiFi network, such as a café or a relative's home network
  • changing the location your connection appears to come from, for example to check news from home while traveling

The VPN has clear limits. It does not make users anonymous, since websites can still recognize visitors through cookies or account logins, and it does not hide browsing history stored on the device. It also covers browsing inside Firefox only. Other apps on the same computer or phone connect normally, and Mozilla points users who want device wide protection to Mozilla VPN, its separate paid subscription.

How to Turn On the Free Firefox VPN

The built-in VPN is available in Firefox on desktop and Android. Mozilla says iOS support is coming soon but has not given a date. To start using it:

  1. Create a Mozilla account, or sign in to an existing one, in Firefox.
  2. On desktop, select the VPN icon in the Firefox toolbar. On Android, open the three dot menu and go to Settings > VPN.
  3. Follow the setup prompts and turn the VPN on.

Availability depends on the region, and Mozilla's Help Center lists the supported countries along with full setup instructions for desktop and Android.

The unlimited period lines up with holiday travel and shopping, when people spend more time on hotel, airport, and café networks. Users who already have the VPN set up do not need to do anything to get the extra data, and users who stopped using it because of the cap can turn it back on and browse for the full period without running out.

The built-in VPN is a lighter option than a full VPN app, since it protects only the browser, but it costs nothing beyond a Mozilla account. That makes it a practical choice for travelers who mainly need to protect browsing on public networks.

Mozilla has not said whether the data cap will return on February 1, 2027, or what the limit will be after the offer ends.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Firefox's Free Built-In VPN Gets Unlimited Data From November 10 Through January 31, 2027 appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Samsung Rolls Out One UI 9 Watch With Wear OS 7 to the Galaxy Watch 8 and Galaxy Watch 8 Classic (2026)
item.description:
Samsung has started rolling out One UI 9 Watch to the Galaxy Watch 8 and Galaxy Watch 8 Classic. The update is based on Google's Wear OS 7 and arrives after about two and a half months of beta testing. The rollout has begun in the US.

The Galaxy Watch 9 and Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 already shipped with Wear OS 7, so this update brings last year's models to the same software.

One UI 9 Watch Update Details

The stable update carries these firmware versions:

  • L320XXU2BZJ7 for the Galaxy Watch 8
  • L500XXU2BZJ7 for the Galaxy Watch 8 Classic

It also includes the October 2026 security patch. The download is reportedly around 2 GB, and it should be much smaller for users who are already running the beta.

The update changes the main parts of the watch experience:

  • a redesigned Galaxy Wearable app on the phone, with a cleaner layout and simpler customization controls
  • a reorganized settings interface on the watch
  • the option to swipe between watch faces from the main screen, without opening a separate customization menu
  • double pinch and shake gestures grouped under a single toggle

Health tracking gets the most new features. Daily Cardio Load shows how much physical activity the wearer gets during the day. Samsung also adds improved sleep vitals monitoring, new heart health insights, and redesigned health charts that make fitness data easier to read.

How to Install One UI 9 Watch on the Galaxy Watch 8

The update is delivered through the phone the watch is paired with. To check for it:

  1. Open the Galaxy Wearable app on the paired phone.
  2. Go to Watch settings > Watch software update.
  3. Select Download and install.

The watch should have enough battery and stay close to the phone while the update installs, since a 2 GB package takes a while to transfer over Bluetooth or WiFi. Owners who run the One UI 9 Watch beta should see a smaller package, since most of the changes are already on their watches.

Owners outside the US may not see the update yet. Samsung usually starts watch updates in one market and adds regions over the following days, so checking again later is the best option for now.

item.title: Windows 11 Version 23H2 Reaches End of Support for Enterprise and Education With the Final KB5131087 Update (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft has ended support for Windows 11 version 23H2 on Enterprise and Education editions. The November 2026 security update, KB5131087, is the last update these editions will receive, according to Microsoft's release notes. Devices that stay on version 23H2 will no longer get monthly security fixes.

Version 23H2 first shipped in October 2023. Home and Pro editions reached the end of support last year, after the usual two years, while Enterprise and Education editions get 36 months of updates.

What the Final Windows 11 23H2 Update Includes

KB5131087 is a cumulative update that rolls in the October security update and an October out of band fix. Microsoft lists these changes:

  • security fixes for vulnerabilities patched this month
  • a fix for adding printers published in Active Directory, which could fail with error 87 after the October update
  • NTLM message signing offered by default for non anonymous connections, to reduce exposure to NTLM relay attacks
  • a fix for a Remote Desktop trusted publisher policy that could not be set through Intune
  • more devices targeted for the new Secure Boot certificates, which replace certificates that began expiring in 2026
  • updated daylight saving time rules for Cuba

Microsoft notes that the Secure Boot certificate rollout continues through Windows Update for eligible devices. That process does not change the end of support date for version 23H2.

How to Stay Supported on Windows 11

Microsoft recommends moving eligible devices to a supported version of Windows 11. Versions 24H2, 25H2, and 26H1 currently receive feature and security updates, and version 26H2 is in the Release Preview channel ahead of a general rollout.

Home and Pro users should already have been offered an upgrade. Enterprise and Education devices may need action from IT if they have not been moved yet:

  1. Install KB5131087 so the device has the final 23H2 security fixes.
  2. Check the version under Settings > System > About.
  3. Upgrade to version 24H2 or later through Windows Update, WSUS, or the organization's management tools.

Microsoft supports each Windows 11 version for two years on Home and Pro and three years on Enterprise and Education. Version 24H2 therefore has one more year of support on Home and Pro and two more years on commercial editions. LTSC and IoT editions follow their own, longer lifecycle and are not affected by this change.

Organizations that skip the upgrade can keep using version 23H2, but the devices will be exposed to any vulnerability patched after November 2026. Schools and companies that still run 23H2 on a large number of machines should plan the move to a newer version as soon as possible.

Microsoft has not announced any paid extended security updates for Windows 11 version 23H2, unlike the program it offers for Windows 10.

item.title: Google's November Pixel Drop Brings Gemini Intelligence to the Pixel 10 and Launches the $29.99 Pixel Tag (2026)
item.description:
Google has released its November Pixel Drop, a feature update for Pixel phones and watches that brings Gemini Intelligence to the Pixel 10 series and launches the Pixel Tag item tracker. Google says the updates start rolling out today and will continue over the coming weeks.

The Pixel Tag goes on sale on November 11 for $29.99, or $99.99 for a four pack.

Gemini Intelligence Comes to the Pixel 10

Gemini Intelligence is now available on Pixel 10 phones. With the Pixel Drop, they get these features:

  • Rambler, an upgraded voice typing mode that removes filler words such as "um" and formats speech into clean text
  • multi step tasks, where Gemini handles jobs such as ordering groceries, booking a ride, or finding a restaurant reservation, now also available in Japan, the UK, and India
  • proactive suggestions, such as sharing an ETA with a tap when someone asks when you will arrive
  • personalized widgets that users can create themselves, such as a spending tracker or a trip countdown that pulls in flight details
  • summaries of long conversations, now in German, French, Spanish, Italian, Hindi, and Traditional Chinese

Google says the Pixel 10a is not included in the Gemini Intelligence update, and the features require setup and are limited to select countries and languages for users 18 and older.

Other Pixel Drop Features and Pixel Tag Details

The Pixel 11 series gets an upgraded Call Screen, where Gemini asks unknown callers why they are calling in a more conversational way and shows a live transcript, so the user can decide when to pick up. Google is also adding:

  1. new custom icon styles that apply across all home screen app icons
  2. Pixel search on Pixel 6 and newer, which finds photos, emails, messages, calendar events, and settings on the phone
  3. HiLight support for Google Messages, so a phone lying face down glows when a favorite contact sends a message
  4. automatic Pixel Watch unlocking when the paired phone is unlocked nearby, coming in the next few weeks
  5. step by step workouts on Pixel Watch 3 and newer

The Pixel Tag is a slim tracker that fits in a wallet and has a battery that lasts more than a year, according to Google. It uses the Find Hub network of more than 1 billion Android devices to locate lost items far away, and Ultra Wideband to show direction and distance when the item is nearby.

Google Fi customers with eligible Pixels also get a new network feature that switches automatically between two US 5G networks and secure WiFi networks.

Pixel owners can check for the update under Settings > System > Software updates, although the rollout is staged and may take a few weeks to reach every device.

Google has not said when the Pixel Tag will be available outside the markets where it launches today.

item.title: EU Proposes Digital Fairness Act to Ban Dark Patterns and Let Users Turn Off Streaks and Autoplay (2026)
item.description:
The European Commission has proposed the Digital Fairness Act, a set of consumer protection rules aimed at "harmful digital practices" in online shopping, social media, apps, and subscriptions.

The proposal would ban dark patterns, let users turn off addictive features such as streaks and autoplay, and make digital subscriptions easier to cancel.

Consumer Protection Commissioner Michael McGrath called the package "the most significant reform of EU consumer protection rules in more than 20 years," noting that the current rules were written before ecommerce and the attention economy took off.

What the Digital Fairness Act Would Change

The proposed rules target practices that large apps and online stores use today. They include:

  • a ban on dark patterns, such as falsely claiming that a product is running low to push a purchase
  • limits on dynamic pricing by ticket sellers
  • a requirement for influencers to disclose when they are paid to promote a product
  • a ban on personalized advertising and pricing that targets minors or uses sensitive data
  • easier cancellation of digital subscriptions
  • a right to reach a human in customer service
  • an option for all users to turn off addictive design features such as video autoplay and streaks

The last point would reach apps such as Duolingo and Strava, which use streaks to keep users coming back every day. The EU already restricts some of these designs for children under its Kids Act, and the new proposal would extend similar choices to adults.

Fines and How the Rules Fit With Existing EU Law

The proposal gives the Commission direct powers to investigate cases with a large scale impact and to fine companies up to 6 percent of their worldwide annual turnover. Companies based outside the EU would have to appoint a local legal representative to work with the authorities.

Executive Vice President Henna Virkkunen said the act is designed to fill gaps between the Digital Services Act, the Digital Markets Act, and the AI Act rather than duplicate them. The Digital Services Act already covers some addictive design on large platforms. The Commission said on Friday that TikTok's "For You" feed breached those rules, and in July it found Meta in breach over similar features on Instagram and Facebook. Both companies could face fines of up to 6 percent of global turnover if the findings are confirmed.

For users in the EU, nothing changes yet. The Digital Fairness Act is a proposal and is not yet law, so apps, ticket sellers, and subscription services can keep their current designs for now. If the rules pass in their current form, the most visible changes would be a setting to switch off streaks and autoplay, simpler cancellation flows, and fewer countdown timers and "only 2 left" banners in online stores.

The Commission has not given a date for when the rules would take effect if they are adopted.

item.title: Microsoft Launches Auto SR on the ROG Xbox Ally X in Handheld Mode, With a 120 FPS Performance Mode Coming (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft has moved Automatic Super Resolution, or Auto SR, out of preview on the ROG Xbox Ally X and Xbox Ally X20 handhelds. The AI upscaling feature now works in handheld mode on battery power, not only when the device is docked, and it supports games running natively at 1080p. Select Copilot+ PC laptops with compatible AMD Ryzen processors get the feature as well.

Auto SR first came to the Xbox Ally X earlier this year, but only for users on a preview version of Windows and only in docked mode.

What Auto SR Does on the Xbox Ally X

Auto SR is Microsoft's own upscaling technology, with the same goal as Nvidia's DLSS and AMD's FSR: higher frame rates with better image quality. The difference is where the work happens. Auto SR runs on the NPU, the AI chip in the handheld's processor, instead of the GPU, which leaves the GPU free to render the game.

The update brings these changes:

  • Auto SR in handheld mode, without the AC adapter connected
  • support for games running natively at 1080p
  • a new Performance Mode that targets up to 120 FPS, up from the previous limit of 60 or 75 FPS
  • Auto HDR support alongside Auto SR

The 1080p handheld support is available now. Performance Mode and Auto HDR are "rolling out with Windows updates," according to Microsoft, so they may take some time to reach every device.

When to Use Auto SR Instead of FSR

Auto SR is most useful for games that do not include FSR or where the built-in FSR option works poorly. Games with a good FSR implementation will usually look closer to the developer's intended image with FSR, since it is integrated into the game itself, while Auto SR works on the finished frame.

Microsoft also warns that "using 1080p in handheld mode (internal screen), performance may not be as optimal as other configurations," but says players will still see visual quality improvements, especially in older games. Owners can keep these points in mind:

  1. Install the latest Windows updates on the handheld to get Performance Mode and Auto HDR when they arrive.
  2. Use FSR first in games that support it well, and switch to Auto SR for games without an upscaler.
  3. Expect the biggest gains in older titles on the internal screen, and on larger screens when docked.

Microsoft originally limited the feature to docked play, saying that is "where Auto SR makes the biggest difference: 1440p-like detail alongside smooth framerates on larger screens." The handheld release makes the NPU in the Xbox Ally X and X20 useful for gaming on the go, not only for AI features in Windows.

Microsoft has not listed which Copilot+ laptops are included or said when Performance Mode will reach all Xbox Ally devices.
